memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Joshua assembled all the tribes of Israel at Shechem. He summoned the elders, leaders, judges and officials of Israel, and they presented themselves before God. Joshua said to all the people, "This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: 'Long ago your ancestors, including Terah the father of Abraham and Nahor, lived beyond the Euphrates River and worshiped other gods.'" — Josh 24:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua gathers all Israel at Shechem for one final, solemn meeting, and they "present themselves before God." This is holy ground. What follows is not merely a speech from an old leader but a message spoken in God's own voice: "This is what the Lord says."

And notice where the story begins. God starts by reminding Israel of an uncomfortable truth: their ancestors, even Abraham's own father, "worshiped other gods." Israel's story did not begin with impressive faith or noble origins. It began with idol-worshippers on the far side of a river.

Why would God begin here? To make one thing unmistakably clear: everything good in Israel's history came from His grace, not their goodness. They were not chosen because they were better; they were chosen because God is gracious.

This is deeply humbling and deeply freeing. None of us comes to God with a spotless past. Like Abraham's family, we were far off, caught up in things that were not God (Eph 2:12-13). But God reaches across the river to call people to Himself. When you are tempted to think God saved you because of something in you, remember Terah. Grace, from first to last, is the whole story. Present yourself before God today, grateful that He called you when you were far away.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you sometimes think God chose you because of something in you?
2. How does it humble you to know grace, not goodness, began your story?
3. What does it mean to "present yourself before God" today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Gracious God, thank You for reaching across the distance to call me when I was far from You. Keep me humble, remembering that grace is the whole of my story. Amen.
